title: ci: the required `Dogfood Regression Gate` goes green when its single-leg `Dogfood Verify CLI` is killed by its own job timeout mid-suite (#16157's split does not reach a 1/1 leg)
body:
Guards a published surface: `objectstack verify --rls` (`@objectstack/cli`) over `examples/app-showcase`, through the required `Dogfood Regression Gate` (triage, R290).

Filing gate: **① class (a), a reproducible defect in a required gate.** reach: the required context `Dogfood Regression Gate` on PR #22596's head `98846f98c7` (run `38021470264`), read by the `domain:spec` seat 3 (#18883) · session `session_01KNKBCRDJCu5tGy3TEbvtrF` while landing #22301 item 5. ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade, the lane and the direction.

## What happened (measured)

- `Dogfood Verify CLI` (job `114123251343`, `timeout-minutes: 20`) reports `started_at` 2026-10-10T03:44:08Z. Its log begins at 04:02:21Z with the runner being provisioned, so about 18 minutes went to waiting for a runner.
- Its step `objectstack verify examples/app-showcase --rls` was still running when the job timeout cancelled it, at 04:04:21Z. The job concluded `cancelled` with the attestation steps `skipped`.
- `Dogfood Regression Gate` ran 21 seconds later and passed. Its log reads:
  - `leg dogfood-verify (single leg) — aggregate result: cancelled`
  - `satisfied (cancelled — run-lifecycle state, #3668; expected attestations: 0)`
  - `Dogfood Regression Gate: satisfied`
- So the required context went green over a CLI verification that never finished. `examples/app-showcase`'s verify pass produced no verdict.

## Why the gate passes it

- `scripts/check-shard-attestation.mjs`' `judge()` splits `cancelled` by count (#16157). With at least one attestation of the leg present, the roster is required and the gate goes red. With zero attestations it passes, as #3668's "superseded matrix".
- A single-leg roster (`dogfood-verify/1`) killed by its own timeout always has zero attestations of that leg. So it is indistinguishable, by that count, from a superseded run, and it passes.
- In this run the run was not superseded: the sibling leg `dogfood` attested 3/3 in the same gate.

## A direction for triage (not a ruling)

Read supersession at the run level rather than per leg. If any other leg of the same gate attested in this run, the run was not superseded, so a zero-attestation `cancelled` leg is a killed leg and the gate goes red, naming it. The same reading applies to every single-leg roster the attestation gates aggregate. ⛔ No new gate script: this is `judge()`'s own blind spot.

**Not measured:**
- how often runner starvation cancels a single-leg job this way;
- whether `Test Core`'s gate aggregates any single-leg roster with the same shape.

Dedupe: open-issue titles in objectstack (127, REST list) matched for `attest`, `cancel`, `aggregat`, `starv`, `timeout` and `dogfood`. One hit is near: #22034 (fetch-depth turning a slow fetch into a cancelled required `Test Core` shard). That is about the cause of a cancellation on a multi-shard leg, not the gate passing a single-leg one. Dedupe words: attestation gate cancelled single leg · dogfood-verify cancelled timeout green · zero attestations superseded run level
